literal: If one renounces desire of an insatiable nature, that very state an unshakable nature will give.
translation: If one renounces desire, whose nature is never to be satisfied, that very moment will yield the changeless state of eternal freedom.
modern: நிறைவடையாத இயல்புடைய ஆசையை ஒருவன் நீக்கினால், அந்த நிலையே அவனுக்கு என்றும் அழியாத நிலைத்த தன்மையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts two kinds of 'iyarkai' (nature or state): the insatiable nature of desire and the changeless nature of liberation. Desire is described as 'ārā iyarkai' because it can never be filled or satisfied; the more it is fed, the more it grows. If a person completely relinquishes this endless desire, they immediately enter 'annilaiyē' (that very state). This shift bestows 'pērā iyarkai', a permanent, unwavering state of peace that never departs.
